## What this does

Makes "green" auditable after the fact, per the contract's four threads:

- **G3b recorded-CI verifier** (`docs/build/tools/verify_recorded_ci.py`, new;
  wired into the `docs` job and `make ci-local`, plus a nightly `--all`
  stage): every `ci:` line a change adds is re-verified against GitHub — each
  recorded run id must resolve to a run on the recorded head sha with a
  `success` conclusion; a bare `ci: pass #N@sha` re-reads the head-bound
  required check-runs; a new Round-11 `done` entry with no `ci:` field fails.
  Unreadable GitHub state is UNKNOWN (exit 5), never green. Stdlib python3,
  read-only `gh api` GETs — it never re-runs anything.
- **G3c external delta** (`ci_boundary.py`, extended): the boundary record now
  carries `origin/main`'s sha, whether the chain tip descends from it
  (`merge-base --is-ancestor`, guarded by `git cat-file -e` —
  `rev-parse --verify` echoes absent objects), PRs merged since the last
  boundary, open off-chain PRs, and per-pair stack ancestry; unresolvable
  facts are `None`/notes, and the line gains a
  `· main: <sha7> descends:yes|no|? merges:N open-other:N` suffix.
- **Flake policy** (`record_policy/ci_flakes.toml`,
  `reports/ci/flake_log.csv`): a required check that fails is re-run at most
  once per head, only when its job + signature match an unexpired allow-list
  entry — `LH-PERF-1` (Lighthouse single-run sampling; expires 2026-11-01,
  tracked by ADR-191) and `PY-SUBSTR-1` (residual cover for the fixed
  assertion defect; expires 2026-10-08). Both attempts are logged; a second
  failure is `flake-exhausted` red; an unwritable log blocks. Never a
  quarantine, skip or loosened assertion (CI-5).
- **Lighthouse stabilisation (ADR-191):** `web/lighthouserc.json`
  `numberOfRuns: 1 → 3`, asserted on the median — ADR-134's budgets and
  thresholds are byte-identical; only the sampling noise floor moves.
- **npm advisory gate (SIG-ENG-042):** per-PR `npm audit --omit=dev` judged at
  `high` by `scripts/ci/npm_audit_gate.py` (driven by
  `scripts/ci/npm_audit_gate.sh`, the same command `ci-local` runs); nightly
  audits the full tree against the dated `npm_audit_allow.toml`. Production
  tree is clean today — `astro` 7.2.4→7.3.5 retires the critical
  GHSA-26w7-cxv4-gfx2 (`devalue` 5.9.2→5.9.4, `undici` 8.10.1→8.11.2 ride the
  lockfile); the four remaining high+ leaf advisories are all `@lhci/cli`
  dev-toolchain transitives under dated `dev-only` entries (`expires
  2026-11-30`, tracking `D-P34.2-1`), cross-checked against the production
  audit so a "dev-only" entry that ships is void. Expired entries fail loudly;
  a malformed or vacuous report is UNKNOWN.
- **Fail-closed leak check:** `test_gcp_project_id_is_env_resolved_not_committed`
  no longer skips when `SIG_GCP_PROJECT` is unset — an unarmed needle is a red
  (OP-07 arms it via `vars.SIG_GCP_PROJECT` in the python + security jobs); it
  prints `candidates`/`evaluated` so a zero-scope scan can never pass
  vacuously.
- **PY-SUBSTR-1 fix:** the curation-timing test walks the row's fields —
  `assert "8.5" not in str(row)` could collide with an ISO timestamp; the row
  must carry no `elapsed`/`timing` key and no `8.5` scalar.
